items.author: 山宗
items.content: 就在刚刚，Lean 和 Mathlib 社区发布联合声明，宣布正式认证 Anthropic 数学家 Levent Alpöge 提交的黎曼猜想形式化证明，并表示对其正确性具有充分信心。 更引人关注的是，Alpöge 此前透露，这项研究由他与 AI 模型 Claude 合作完成。在证明接近终点时，Claude 展现出的数学推理能力，甚至超出了他的预期。 11 月 20 日，Alpöge 在个人网站公布研究成果，宣称解决了著名的黎曼猜想（Riemann Hypothesis），同时取得了涉及广义黎曼猜想（Generalized Riemann Hypothesis）的结果。 它涉及黎曼 ζ 函数非平凡零点的分布，核心命题是所有非平凡零点的实部是否都等于 1/2。由于这一问题与素数分布密切相关，过去一个多世纪，无数数学家尝试攻克，却始终未能找到严格证明。 马斯克也发文感叹，证明黎曼猜想能够让大量此前依赖该猜想成立的数学结论摆脱条件限制，成为无条件成立的定理，并称其为超级智能取得的又一项惊人成就。 他曾尝试让 Claude 将证明整理成人类能够阅读的文字版本，结果生成的草稿超过 25 万页，庞大到连他本人都认为难以阅读。如此惊人的篇幅，甚至被部分网友戏称为一场针对数学界的「DDoS 攻击」。

items.content: 就在刚刚，Anthropic 数学家 Levent Alpöge 在个人网站发布声明，宣布自己与 Claude 合作，找到了著名的黎曼猜想（Riemann Hypothesis）的证明。 更夸张的是，Alpöge 声称，他们甚至进一步证明了难度更高、适用范围更广的广义黎曼猜想（Generalized Riemann Hypothesis）。 有意思的是，Alpöge 此次没有发布传统意义上的完整数学论文，而是公开了一套使用 Lean 形式化证明语言编写的代码，试图让计算机验证整个数学推理过程。 结果临近终点，Claude 的推理速度已经快到让他难以跟上。他甚至用诗一般的语言感叹，Claude 在终点线附近飞翔、起舞、闪耀，而自己只能惊叹于眼前发生的一切。 素数就是只能被 1 和自身整除的正整数，例如 2、3、5、7、11。它们是整数世界的重要基础，但具体会在哪里出现，看起来始终缺乏直观规律。 看起来只是一个简单的数学表达式，却关系到素数分布的精确程度，以及现代数论中大量重要结论。过去 167 年，无数顶尖数学家试图证明它，期间诞生了大量数学理论和研究工具，却始终没人能够给出获得普遍认可的完整证明。

items.author: 郑廷旭
items.content: 11 月 20 日，Anthropic 数学家 Levent Alpöge 在个人网站发布声明，称自己与 Claude 合作找到了黎曼猜想的证明，并表示同一方法还可以推广至广义黎曼猜想。目前，这一成果尚未经过独立验证。 黎曼猜想是数学界著名的「千禧年七大难题」之一，由德国数学家黎曼于 1859 年提出，涉及素数的分布规律。Alpöge 此次公开了一份 4 页说明，以及分成 14 个压缩包的 Lean 形式化证明文件，供其他研究者核查。 Alpöge 介绍，这项研究借鉴了数论中已有的证明思路，通过串联名为 theta 提升的数学变换，模拟传统方法中的「重数」作用。其中，Claude 提出让变换链的长度随求和范围的平方根增长，成为推进证明的关键思路之一。他表示，Claude 在研究后期的推进速度已经超过自己，接下来还将整理一份便于数学家理解的人类可读证明。 菲尔兹奖得主陶哲轩也于 11 月 20 日在个人博客提及此事。他指出，Alpöge 使用 AI 生成了一份规模庞大、仅以 Lean 代码呈现的广义黎曼猜想证明，理解和消化这份成果仍需要时间，但至少可以与人类作者沟通，协助完成这一过程。 目前，数学界仍需确认这些 Lean 文件能否独立通过校验，以及形式化定理是否准确对应黎曼猜想。陶哲轩的回应也不意味着证明已经获得认可。 三星电子 11 月 20 日宣布，由崔元俊接掌负责 Galaxy 手机的移动体验业务，卢泰文继续领导设备体验部门，并与负责半导体部门的全永铉共同担任 CEO。崔元俊自 2025 年 3 月起担任移动体验业务 COO，曾负责推动 Galaxy S26 和 Galaxy Z Fold8 系列上市。

items.content: 今天，知名半导体和 AI 研究机构 SemiAnalysis 在 X 上发了一张写给 Google DeepMind 主席 Demis Hassabis 的《向 Google 道歉专用表》。 理由一栏勾了包括「我只看了 X 上大家的消息」、「我那在 Anthropic 工作的室友，说服我相信 Gemini 已经完了」和「我没有阅读模型卡」等原因。最有意思的是最后一行：「Demis，关于 Gemini 4，我们错了。我们只想撤回一个词。」 他们从自己当初的标题里划掉了一个 is：Gemini is cooked。一句「Gemini 完了」，变成了「Gemini 这回真做出了点东西」。 事件的起因是 SemiAnalysis 在今年 8 月份发布了一篇文章，通篇都在讲 Google 自从去年 11 月短暂领先之后，就再也没有发布任何让人激动的模型，几乎是处在了掉队中的状态。 当时他们分析 DeepMind 的强化学习团队走了不少人，内部的算力又没分配好，对 Google 下了一个相当重的判断： 照这样下去，Google 当然还会继续发模型，但再一次达到行业最高水平的概率，已经「降到了零」。 报告发出不到两个月，谷歌就公布了 Gemini 4 Argon，接着 10 月底发布 Carbon、11 月 12 号推出 Hydrogen，18 号发布 Neon，短短 8 天的时间，接连推出了 3 款模型，其中 Carbon 的表现当时还来到了 Artificial Analysis 的综合能力榜首。

items.content: When Notable Capital poured roughly 10% of the U.S. portion of its $1 billion-plus fund into Anthropic’s Series E, many limited partners were perplexed by the massive bet. Claude’s maker was still trailing its biggest rival, OpenAI, and DeepSeek had released its R1 model just weeks earlier, threatening to overtake closed-source competitors. Moreover, at $61.5 billion, Anthropic’s valuation was by far the highest that the predominantly early-stage venture firm had invested at in its 25-year history. But investors at Notable, formerly known as GGV Capital before its 2024 split from its China operations, were confident in Anthropic’s future. A team that included managing partners Hans Tung and Glenn Solomon and principal Dan Cahana crunched the numbers and found that developers were increasingly favoring Claude over ChatGPT, using Claude 70% of the time, a reversal from the previous year. “We just knew that for AI, the developer is at the center because they’re the early adopters,” Tung, a co-founder of the firm, told TechCrunch. Having navigated the complexities of U.S.-China relations firsthand, Notable was also convinced that “mission-critical” work would always require U.S.-based, closed-source models, Tung said. items.title: OpenAI’s chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development
items.description: To establish a speed limit on AI development, you need to agree on how to measure speed.
items.author: Anthony Ha
items.content: A new blog post from OpenAI’s chief scientist Jakub Pachocki discusses potential limits on AI development, with a focus on a measurement called perplexity. Slowing AI development became a particularly hot topic after a former OpenAI and Anthropic researcher said the companies were “gambling with our lives,” and even Anthropic’s IPO filing suggested that the technology could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to society.” Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei then published a plan to “pace the frontier,” seemingly endorsed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Among other things, Amodei called for companies to agree to “common safety standards as well as limits on the rate of unchecked AI progress.” But to establish a speed limit on AI development, you need to agree on how you measure speed. Pachocki’s post — described by Altman as “the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while” — suggests perplexity (not to be confused with the company of the same name ) could be that measurement. In Pachochki’s argument, benchmarks that focus on AI’s “downstream capabilities” have quickly become outdated as the technology advances. But perplexity — which “measures how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions” — has remained “informative.” Pachochki’s post includes a chart of how the perplexity of OpenAI’s models has fallen since GPT 3.5.

items.title: Signal restricts mobile screenshots as it confronts ‘existential threat’ of AI surveillance
items.description: Signal is limiting users' ability to take screenshots in both its Android and iOS apps.
items.author: Anthony Ha
items.content: Signal announced Friday that it’s limiting users’ ability to take screenshots within the secure messaging app — a response to what President Meredith Whittaker described as the “existential threat” of operating systems that integrate agentic AI. Whittaker wrote that by giving AI agents the ability to “scan” the information on users’ screens, Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS “are undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.” “Now, in service of AI agentic capabilities, your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” she said. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.” Signal already sought to limit these risks by blocking screenshots of its Windows app by default. Now it’s adding similar restrictions in Android and iOS. That said, users can disable this setting if they wish, which Whittaker said would “break our privacy guarantees.” She also admitted this is an “incomplete” solution, as it doesn’t “address other more sneaky ways AI agents could potentially access application data.” Get an Early Peek at the Next TechCrunch Disrupt Disrupt, Startup Battlefield, and more will return next year, and you can be at the front of the line. items.title: Daniel Ek backs AI researcher’s fusion power startup. Here’s what they’re building.
items.description: Spotify founder Daniel Ek is backing Europa Fusion, a fusion power startup founded by an AI researcher. Here's what the startup is building.
items.author: Tim De Chant
items.content: Spotify founder Daniel Ek is backing Europa Fusion, a stealthy fusion power startup founded by an AI researcher who is taking a different approach to developing a fusion power plant. The U.K.-based startup was founded in February, though sources told TechCrunch that the founder, Nantas Nardelli, has been working on the idea for longer. The people asked not to be identified because the information isn’t public. Bloomberg first reported Ek’s backing of Europa Fusion. Nardelli has extensive experience in the AI world, having previously worked at Google DeepMind, Facebook AI Research, and Microsoft Research Cambridge. Recently, he was head of machine learning at Pacific Fusion , the fusion power startup based in Fremont, California. Pacific Fusion recently broke ground on a demonstration facility in New Mexico. Like most fusion startups of its size , Pacific Fusion leans heavily on physical devices to test its theories and improve its simulations. Nardelli apparently didn’t agree with the focus on hardware, instead thinking that fusion startups should invest in a more simulation- and data-heavy approach, a source familiar with his thinking told TechCrunch. Like Pacific Fusion, Europa Fusion will pursue a pulsed-power approach to fusion. Pulsed-power reactors use massive, perfectly timed surges of electrical current to compress fuel targets until the atoms inside fuse and release energy.

items.title: AI claimed a solution to the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis — and a human did, too
items.description: Mathematicians are having their minds blown by the latest AI-driven result — and there's a competing human solution, too.
items.author: Tim Fernholz
items.content: It’s a big week for Levent Alpöge: The mathematician saw his employer, Anthropic, become the first publicly traded frontier AI lab. He also appears to have solved one of the most important problems in mathematics. “The precise timing is horrible,” he wrote in an essay announcing his findings and describing how he messaged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei last Sunday night to ask how to announce that he had found a Lean-compilable solution to the Riemann hypothesis, which dates back to 1859 and is among the Millennium Prize math problems. The hypothesis conjectures that there is a hidden structure underlying the appearance of prime numbers. If the claimed result holds true, we’re entering sublime-mysteries-of-the-universe territory. Maybe the best way to understand how exciting this is to the mathematics community is to watch the experts puzzling through the result in a chat on Zulip . Mathematicians like Chris Birkbeck, a number theorist at the University of East Anglia, are posting thoughts like this … The cohomology bound is proved by what looks like an automorphy-lifting argument. It genuinely uses the existence of Galois representations attached to regular algebraic, polarized cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n over CM fields, along with base change, Jacquet–Shalika, Clozel’s purity, Bernstein–Zelevinsky, the main theorem of CM, Deligne–Ribet and more. For my part, I tapped out of mathematics at college calculus, so I can’t help decode exactly what that means.
